# Replicated triangle guards: the sharp individual capacity floor is one third

This is an exact best-menu, full-convex-field obstruction. In continuous dimension two, allowing the integer dimension to vary, the universal individual-source capacity lower bound1/3 is sharp in the attained pure outward-smoothed interface. In particular the proposed universal individual1/e floor is FALSE. The example is far above the OC target and has only one actual deepest source, leaving a large unused parity budget.

The geometric construction and the exact all-angle triangle calculation originate in `candidate 2ab56d1c26a2c4f9`. The replication and the sharp asymptotic conclusion below are separate additions. The proof is included here to track all constants and quantifiers.

## 1. Definitions and theorem

Let L>=1 be an integer, set n=3L and d=2, and fix sigma=1/4. Let T be a regular triangle with centroid0, vertices v_0,v_1,v_2, volume V, and barycentric coordinates lambda_0,lambda_1,lambda_2. Put

    D_i=(1-sigma)v_i+sigma T,    v=|D_i|=sigma^2 V.

Index the standard base vectors of R^(3L) by e_(i,r), with i=0,1,2 and1<=r<=L. Take the actual convex body

    C_L=conv( ({0}xT) union
              union_(i,r) ({-e_(i,r),e_(i,r)}xD_i) ).

Its complete integer base set is

    P={0} union {+-e_(i,r)}.

Indeed its projection is the unit crosspolytope, whose only lattice points are precisely these. Each extreme base has the prescribed fiber D_i. Every convex combination landing at base0 has its continuous coordinate in T, so the central fiber is exactly T. All fibers are positive two-dimensional, and C_L has full dimension3L+2.

Use the actual pooled within-fiber covariance norm Gamma_L and the uniform outward kernel

    Psi(t)=min(1,max(0,1+t)).

A cap through the mark Y has value

    integral Psi( [N·(w-Y)]/[h Gamma_L(u)] ) dmu(w),

where N=(a,u), u is its continuous normal, and mu is the finite fiber-area sum. Pure-base caps remain closed halfspaces. Let

    w=h Gamma_L(grad lambda_i),   0<w<=1/100.          (1)

The value is independent of i by symmetry. At the unique deepest source Y=0, an active response menu is a probability law on actual active caps whose coarea-weighted continuous normal averages to zero. Its boundary profile W is the corresponding average of their smoothed capture integrands.

For a nonnegative continuous physical field Phi(n_b,z,x), convex in(z,x) for each continuous boundary normal n_b, define its efficiency as

    EFF(W,Phi) = integral W Phi dS / integral Phi dS,

when the denominator is positive. Here dS is the SUM of the ordinary edge-length measures of all sampled fibers, with their continuous outer normals recorded. There is no ambient surface-measure substitution.

The theorem is:

* The unique deepest point is0 in the central fiber.
* Every actual active cap has one of the three canonical continuous directions grad lambda_i, and every active response menu gives each direction TOTAL weight1/3.
* For EVERY such menu and EVERY admissible field,

      EFF(W,Phi)
        <= 1/3 + (1/9+w/3)/(1+L).                  (2)

* The supremum over menus and fields is at least1/3. Consequently its infimum across this family, and the universal individual-source floor in d=2, is exactly1/3.

Already L=3, n=9, gives

    EFF <=13/36+w/12 <=1303/3600 <4/11 <1/e.         (3)

The final inequality uses e<11/4. Thus (3) is an explicit finite-dimensional all-menu counterexample to the individual1/e assertion.

## 2. Actual covariance and the exact own triangle minimum

Every guard has within-fiber covariance sigma^2 Sigma_T. The pooled covariance is therefore

    Sigma_L=kappa_L Sigma_T,
    kappa_L=(1+6L sigma^4)/(1+6L sigma^2)>0.           (4)

The total mass is M=V(1+6L sigma^2). This uses the actual guard centroids only to center their within-fiber covariances; no between-fiber covariance is inserted.

For completeness, normalize a nonzero continuous functional u so that its maximum vertex value on the centroid-zero triangle is M_u>0. When the through-centroid cap retains one vertex, write its three vertex values as

    M_u,  -(1+s)M_u/2,  -(1-s)M_u/2,
    |s|<1.

Its ordinary own cap fraction is4/(9-s^2). Its covariance width divided by M_u is

    eta sqrt(1+s^2/3),   eta=3w/2.

For |s|<=1/2 the entire width strip remains a one-vertex cut under (1). Averaging the exact displaced vertex-cap area gives

    [4/(9-s^2)]
      [1+eta sqrt(1+s^2/3)+eta^2(1+s^2/3)/3].       (5)

Every factor is strictly increasing in s^2, so the only minimum in this range is s=0. For other one-vertex directions the ordinary area is at least16/35, and outward smoothing only increases it. Two-vertex through-centroid caps have ordinary area at least1/2: their complementary one-vertex cap has edge ratios a,b<=1 with1/a+1/b=3, hence ab<=1/2.

The canonical value is

    q_h/V=4/9+2w/3+w^2/3 <16/35                    (6)

for w<=1/100. Thus the ONLY own smoothed minimizing continuous directions are the three canonical vertex directions, for all angles. Formula (5) and the strict comparisons also cover boundary directions by continuity.

## 3. A global outside quota for every ambient normal

For any u choose a maximum vertex i, so u(v_i)=M_u>0. Since the three vertex values sum to zero and are at most M_u, every vertex value is at least-2M_u. Every point x of D_i therefore satisfies

    u(x)>=(1-sigma)M_u-2sigma M_u
          =(1-3sigma)M_u>0.                         (7)

Consider one reflected pair of its guards at+-e_(i,r). For the same x in D_i the two margins are

    a_(i,r)+u(x),   -a_(i,r)+u(x).

Their sum is positive. At least one margin is positive and hence has capture value one; the other capture is nonnegative. Integrating proves that this pair costs at least v for EVERY real a_(i,r). There are L independent pairs of the maximizing vertex, so every nonvertical ambient cap through the central centroid has outside mass at least Lv.

For the canonical i direction use the scale u=lambda_i-1/3. On its own guards, u>=2/3-sigma>0. Choose each corresponding base coefficient sufficiently large to capture one guard completely and miss the reflected guard. On every other guard u<=sigma-1/3=-1/12, so base coefficient zero misses it beyond the entire strip because w<=1/100. The independence of the base axes makes all these choices simultaneous. Thus each canonical cap attains exactly outside mass Lv.

Combined with (6), the actual minimum over ALL ambient nonvertical normals and all base tilts is

    Q=q_h+Lv.                                        (8)

A pure-base closed cap through0 includes T and at least one member of every axis pair, so it has mass at least V+3Lv>Q. Pure-base directions are therefore inactive.

Every noncentral base is exposed in the complete base crosspolytope and has depth at most v<Q. The three canonical active caps at0 have positively balanced continuous normals and span the continuous plane. For any nonzero displacement in T one of those cap thresholds strictly increases; its proper own strip first loses mass strictly, and threshold monotonicity preserves strict loss thereafter. Hence0 is the unique deepest point in the entire mixed set.

## 4. Equality classifies EVERY active menu

Equality in (8) requires equality in both the own lower bound and the outside quota. Hence the continuous direction must be canonical i. Each of its L matching reflected pairs already costs at least v, so equality forces each pair to have cost exactly v and all other guards to have zero cost.

For a matching pair, (7) holds pointwise. If one capture value were strictly between zero and one on a set of positive area, the other would be one there and the pair integral would exceed v. Thus both integrands are saturated. Their continuous affine margins and the fixed sign of the base coefficient show that one whole guard is captured and the other is missed. The same conclusion holds on their boundaries by continuity. All nonmatching guards are identically missed. In particular ALL active caps have zero outside strip coarea.

The canonical own coareas and covariance widths are equal by triangle symmetry. The three canonical normals have their unique positive balanced dependence with equal weights. It follows that EVERY response menu, including arbitrary splitting among different base tilts, gives each continuous direction TOTAL weight1/3.

Only the i direction can capture a point on an i guard. Therefore

    0<=W<=1/3 on EVERY endpoint boundary.              (9)

This bound is pointwise and uniform over all active menus. On the central triangle, all menus have the same profile

    W_h(x)=(1/3) sum_i Psi((lambda_i(x)-1/3)/w).       (10)

## 5. Exact own-edge bound for every convex field

On a central edge use its affine coordinate s in[0,1]. One barycentric coordinate is zero, so under (1),

    W_h(s)=(1/3)[Psi((s-1/3)/w)+Psi((2/3-s)/w)].

It is symmetric under s->1-s and nondecreasing on[0,1/2]. Its mean is

    integral_0^1 W_h(s)ds =4/9+w/3.                  (11)

For a convex nonnegative function f on this edge, F(s)=f(s)+f(1-s) is nonincreasing on[0,1/2]. To prove this monotonicity directly, a smaller symmetric pair of points is a mean-preserving contraction of a larger pair; convexity decreases their summed values. Thus W_h and F are oppositely monotone on the half interval. The elementary covariance identity

    2 length(J)^2 Cov_J(A,B)
       =integral_J integral_J(A(s)-A(t))(B(s)-B(t))dsdt

shows their covariance is nonpositive. Consequently

    integral_edge W_h f <=(4/9+w/3) integral_edge f.   (12)

Apply (12) at each source-edge normal to the corresponding restriction of Phi, and sum. If I is the total central boundary-field integral,

    N_own <=(4/9+w/3) I.                             (13)

No boundedness ratio for f is assumed; (12) includes arbitrarily concentrating convex fields.

## 6. Replicated contact costs on every source edge

Each source edge has two endpoint vertices. For each such vertex there are L reflected guard pairs whose parallel facet is the corresponding edge segment of relative length sigma. At a point x on that segment, full ambient convexity gives

    Phi(n_b,-e_(i,r),x)+Phi(n_b,e_(i,r),x)
       >=2Phi(n_b,0,x).

Summing these inequalities on the actual shared edge segments, over all L pairs and both endpoint vertices, gives for each source edge

    E_edge >=2L |edge|
      [integral_0^sigma f(s)ds+integral_(1-sigma)^1 f(s)ds].

For every convex f the bracket is at least2sigma integral_0^1 f. Indeed F(s)=f(s)+f(1-s) is nonincreasing on[0,1/2], so its average over[0,sigma] is at least its average over the whole half interval. Thus, after summing source edges,

    E >=4L sigma I = L I.                            (14)

Here E is the TOTAL guard boundary-field integral; extra guard facets only increase it. Every comparison uses the same continuous normal on coincident parallel facets. Boundary vertices have zero length. The argument does not identify different base fibers or replace their surface sum by the boundary of their convex hull.

## 7. Capacity, the explicit 1/e failure, and sharpness

By (9),(13), the full numerator satisfies

    N <=(4/9+w/3)I +(1/3)E.

Since E>=LI, division by I+E yields (2); the case I=0 follows directly from (9). This proves the bound for EVERY active menu and EVERY normal-dependent convex field.

For L=3 and w<=1/100, the upper bound is1303/3600. It is strictly below4/11 because1303*11=14333<14400=4*3600. The elementary exponential-series estimate e<11/4 gives4/11<1/e. This proves (3) exactly.

Conversely select one canonical active cap from each direction, with response weight1/3. For any one selected cap with affine margin m, take the normal-independent physical field[m]_+. On its positive set that cap's smoothed capture equals one, so the menu profile is at least1/3 there. Its boundary integral is positive because the proper own cap contains a positive-length boundary portion on which m>0. Hence the efficiency is at least1/3.

Let L tend to infinity with w fixed in(0,1/100]. The upper bound (2) tends to1/3 and the matching lower bound holds for every L. More generally, in the attained d=2 interface any balanced active response law admits a finite balanced menu of at most three caps by the elementary planar convex-hull theorem. One of its response weights is at least1/3, and its positive-margin hinge pays that weight. Thus1/3 is the universal individual-source best-menu floor and this family shows it is sharp when the integer dimension is unrestricted.

## 8. Scope and consequence for the OC search

The construction has one source and n=3L integer dimensions. It has enormous unused source-parity capacity and no claim of global body stationarity. Its depth is not below the desired OC level. It therefore does not challenge OC, saturated-source payment, or a shared allocation using the full parity budget.

It DOES close the suggested dimension-free individual1/e shortcut. Even after optimizing over every actual active menu and every nonnegative normal-dependent convex physical field, a single source may approach the elementary three-cap hinge floor1/3. A proof of OC by this variational interface must use source-sharing, parity slack, or information from an actual body minimum beyond individual active-cap geometry.

# Replicated triangle guards: the sharp individual capacity floor is one third

**Replicated nonnegative physical-field capacity falls below 1/e**

In the attained pure outward-smoothed interface, the replicated triangle-guard family has d=2,n=3L,L>=1,sigma=1/4. For 0<w<=1/100 every actual balanced menu and every admissible nonnegative convex physical field of positive boundary cost has efficiency at most 1/3+(1/9+w/3)/(1+L). At L=3 this is at most 1303/3600<1/e. The same attained interface has universal individual-source best-menu floor 1/3, approached by this family as L tends to infinity. This is an auxiliary nonnegative-field capacity result, not a bound for ordinary halfspace depth.

Scope limits: Positive-width outward-smoothed capacity model only; not ordinary halfspace depth or a counterexample to OC.
